situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Sensitivities

Target audience: University students (Calculus I beginners)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of Rate of Change

Lecture lines:
Slope is simply rise over run.
Picture a secant line between two points.
It measures average speed of motion.

Planned animations:
Display text: 'Rate of Change'. Create a line plot representing a function y=f(x) in #FFFFFF.
Draw a secant line between two points on the curve in #FF00FF.
Animate the secant line as the points move closer together.

Section: section_2 — The Transformation: From Secant to Tangent

Lecture lines:
Imagine a magnifying glass on a curve.
Shrink the interval towards zero.
The secant line becomes a tangent.
This is the derivative's geometric form.
Zooming reveals the curve's instant slope.

Planned animations:
Draw a static secant line between points A and B.
Highlight the distance between x values as delta x #00FFFF.
Shrink delta x to zero, transforming the secant into a tangent line in #FFFF00.

Section: section_3 — The Derivative as a Sensitivity Operator

Lecture lines:
Think of derivatives as sensitivity operators.
They transform functions into rate indicators.
Like a robot's velocity command.

Planned animations:
Display the function f(x) and its slope at a point x.
Flash the tangent line in #00FF00 to emphasize slope sensitivity.
Show a small change in x resulting in a small change in f.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the Derivative Function

Lecture lines:
Map each point to its steepness.
The derivative reflects the curve's change.
It visualizes the sensitivity function.

Planned animations:
Plot the original function f(x) in #FFFFFF.
Draw the derivative function f'(x) in #FF6600 beneath the graph.
Animate the tangent slope tracing out the f'(x) curve.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis & Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Derivative equals dynamic local slope.
It maps inputs to local sensitivities.
Use it to predict system changes.

Planned animations:
Show f(x), tangent, and derivative in a unified geometric frame.
Group all three elements into a single triangular layout.
Fade all elements to #FFFFFF for a final synthesis.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Conclusion", ["Derivative equals dynamic local slope.", "It maps inputs to local sensitivities.", "Use it to predict system changes."])
        
        # Define elements
        f_x = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE)
        slope = MathTex("f'(x)", color=YELLOW)
        sensitivity = MathTex("\\text{Sensitivity}", color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(f_x, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(slope, "B5")
        self.play(FadeIn(f_x), FadeIn(slope))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(sensitivity, "E4")
        self.play(FadeIn(sensitivity))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Final synthesis
        group = VGroup(f_x, slope, sensitivity)
        self.play(group.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)
